speakers.name: David Provost
speakers.evidence: Public speaker thanks 'David Provost' for BTAB efforts (row 7); S1 runs the meeting throughout and is later addressed as 'David' by other members (row 162).

speakers.name: Joan Shannon
speakers.evidence: Addressed as 'Doctor. Shannon' before speaking (row 73) and as 'Joan' when answered by Terry (row 77).

speakers.name: Terry Dorman
speakers.evidence: S1 asks 'Terry, do you want to touch base on...' and S7 answers directly (rows 49-50).

speakers.name: Stephen Barraclough
speakers.evidence: S1 says 'Stephen, anything to add on sales process and change?' and S8 responds as the manager (rows 54-55); later addressed as 'Mister Barroclaw' (row 174).

chapters.title: Call to Order and Agenda Approval
chapters.summary: The chair calls the meeting to order, the agenda is approved without amendment, and the July minutes are approved.

chapters.title: Public Forum: Carolyn Bates on KBTL/Shores Proposal
chapters.summary: Carolyn Bates proposes advancing KBTL and Shores (an Indiana telecom) together as bidders, suggesting Shores provide financing while KBTL runs BT locally, with future buyback options.

chapters.title: Public Forum: Deb Flanders on Local Ownership
chapters.summary: New BT customer Deb Flanders expresses concern that rates and service will worsen if BT is sold to an outside corporation, citing KBTL's financial plan and the City Market co-op precedent.

chapters.title: Public Forum: Kit Andrews and the KBTL Business Plan
chapters.summary: Kit Andrews presents a petition of 24 downtown business owners supporting KBTL and compares KBTL's conservative financial projections to City Market's successful co-op launch.

chapters.title: Sale Process Update: Bidders and the HBC/Shores Deal
chapters.summary: David and Terry update the board that the council will narrow bidders to two after a meeting Monday, and note Shores recently acquired HBC (Hiawatha), the Winona-based telecom that originally advised BT's turnaround.

chapters.title: Q&A: Ting's Name, DNF Relationships, and Stephen's Future
chapters.summary: Board members ask about Ting keeping the BT name, ongoing relationships between Dorman & Faucette and bidders, and whether Stephen Barraclough has spoken with any bidders about his future role; he declines to speculate publicly.

chapters.title: Data Privacy and Protection Discussion
chapters.summary: Joan Shannon raises concerns about how future owners will handle customer data; Stephen and Jeremy Bacher explain BT's current policies (no data selling, encrypted billing system) and agree industry best practices should continue.

chapters.title: Council Recommendation and Attendance at Monday's Meeting
chapters.summary: David notes BTAB's recommendations have been sent to and released by the council, and encourages members to attend Monday's council meeting to share views.

chapters.title: Management Update: Subscribers, Staffing, and Financials
chapters.summary: Stephen reports 7,224 subscribers (up 35% year-over-year), staffing shortages in customer service due to the pending sale, softness in business (not residential) demand, and on-plan build-out including the new North End and Ethan Allen Mall storefront opening November 1.

chapters.title: Innovation Week and BTV Ignite Preview
chapters.summary: Stephen previews next week's Innovation Week events (Mont Hack, Tech Jam, FreshTrax) organized under BTV Ignite, including a keynote from Bill Wallace and participation from the Governor and Mayor.

chapters.title: Closing Remarks and Thanks
chapters.summary: David, Joan, and another councilor thank Dorman & Faucette and the BT management team for their work over the seven-year process; Stephen thanks the BT team and BTAB, expressing optimism about BT's future before the meeting adjourns.

BTAB members attend Monday's council meeting to share their thoughts on the sale.

bullets.text: Monthly Burlington Telecom Advisory Board (BTAB) meeting to hear public comment, review the sale process for Burlington Telecom, and receive a management update.
Multiple public speakers voiced strong support for keeping BT locally owned via Keep Burlington Telecom Local (KBTL), citing rate stability, service quality, and community control.
The city council plans to narrow the sale bidders to two after a meeting the following Monday, with Dorman & Faucette then negotiating final terms.
Shores (a bidder) recently acquired HBC/Hiawatha, the Winona, MN company that originally advised BT's turnaround and which BT modeled itself on.
Ting has indicated willingness to keep the Burlington Telecom name, though not necessarily permanently.

Stephen Barraclough declined to say which bidder he'd want to work for, citing a desire not to influence the process, but confirmed his interest in continuing to shape BT's future if the new owner shares his vision.
BT's current policy is not to sell customer data; billing data is encrypted and isolated from the public internet, though public WiFi traffic carries standard internet risks.
First quarter subscriber growth was strong (7,224 subscribers, up 35% YoY), though staffing losses in customer service and some business-client hesitancy are emerging due to sale uncertainty.
The agenda and July 12 minutes were approved without amendment.
BTAB's prior recommendations on bidders have already been sent to and released by the city council as part of the public record.
Whether and how customer data protections (encryption, privacy) will be addressed in future ownership negotiations remains unresolved.
Whether BT staff will be given a formal opportunity to share their views with the city council before the sale decision.
City council meets Monday to narrow bidders to two finalists.
Dorman & Faucette will continue negotiating clarifications with remaining bidders, including on data protection and naming commitments.
BT will open its Ethan Allen Mall storefront around November 1 and continue North End build-out.
Innovation Week (BTV Ignite events including Mont Hack, Tech Jam, FreshTrax) occurs next week.
